Next, in a non stick pan, pour the condensed milk and desiccated coconut. Turn the heat down to low and cook it, stirring continuously. \n 3. In about 5 minutes (or less, sometimes) the mixture will begin to turn thick almost like a dough. If you are adding in the rose syrup, now is the time. \n 4. Once the mixture reaches dough like consistency, you can stop cooking it. Add rose syrup and mix uniformly. \n 5. Take the mixture off the heat and let it rest for until cools down a bit and is easier to handle with your bare palms. \n 6. Grease your palm well with ghee or butter. Pinch a lemon sized coconut ladoo dough mixture and press it well between your palms and then roll it into a rough round ladoo. \n 7. Flatten the ladoo dough slightly and make an depression in the center with your thumb. Add a teaspoon of ground pistachios to the centre. \n 8. Roll once again, encasing the ground pistachio inside the coconut laddoo, into perfect rounds. \n 9. Finally, roll the ladoo in desiccated coconut and set it aside. Repeat until you have used up all the coconut ladoo dough. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve them immediately or store the laddoos in an airtight box in the fridge for about 2-3 days. \n [EOS]

Place the poppy seeds on a platter and roll the churma ladoos on the poppy seeds to coat them evenly. \n 9. Allow the ladoos to set for an hour before serving. You can store the Churma Ladoos in air tight canisters for a couple of weeks in the refrigerator and warm them for a few seconds in the microwave before serving. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve the Churma Ladoo Recipe (Atta/Whole Wheat Ladoo) as a dessert after your delicious meal of , , . \n [EOS]

Remove from oil and place it on a kitchen towel to absorb excess oil. \n 10. Once it completely cools, store in air tight container and enjoy them for a longer time. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve Vivatta Whole Wheat Flour Murukku with hot , during your tea time break. \n [EOS]

[BOS] \n **Title:** Homemade Coconut Milk Recipe \n  \n **Cuisine:** Indian | **Diet:** Vegetarian | **Time:** 10 mins prep, 0 mins cook \n  \n **Ingredients:** \n - Fresh coconut \n  \n **Instructions:** \n 1. first grate the coconut using a shredder and keep aside. \n 2. If you have a juicer attachment in your mixer grinder, then it is really convenient to extract the coconut milk. Fix the extraction blade and the juice attachment. \n 3. Add the grated coconut and 1 cup of warm water and blend to extract the coconut milk. This will be the first extraction. You can add more water and then extract more coconut milk after the first extraction. \n 4. If you don't have the extraction blade, then place the grated coconut in a blender jar and add 1 cup warm water and blend till the coconut is ground well. \n 5. Cover the pan with a wet muslin cloth or a towel and place it at a warm place to rise for about 45 minutes or until the rolls have doubled up in size. \n 14. In a bowl, add flour and salt. Give it a mix. \n 3. In a separate bowl, add the lemon juice to the cold water and keep aside. \n 4. Now, add the frozen grated butter to the flour and mix it quickly with the help of a fork. Do not use your hands, otherwise butter will start melting. \n 5. Start adding the cold water, a tablespoon at a time, and keep mixing with the fork. Then bring it all together with your hands. You will have a big rough ball of dough. , Put the dough on a flat surface and lightly pat it with your hand. Then wrap it in a cling film and keep it in fridge to rest for a minimum of 1 hour. You can prepare this dough in advance also. \n 6. You can keep it in the fridge for up to 3 days and up to 2 months in the freezer. , The next step is to make the filling. In a non- stick pan, heat a teaspoon of oil and then add chopped mushrooms, zucchini, and a teaspoon of salt. \n 7. Saut it for about 5-10 minutes or until the water released from the vegetables dries up. Take the vegetables from the pan, pu it in a bowl and keep aside. \n 8. Now, in the same pan, add butter and as soon the butter heats up, add garlic and onion. When the onion becomes golden brown, add the saut ed mushrooms and zucchini. , Next, add salt and thyme, and cook for a minute. Remove from heat and keep aside to cool down. \n 9. The final step is to prepare the puffs. To begin with, put your oven on preheat at 200 C and line your baking tray with parchment paper. \n 10. Next, add egg and milk in a bowl and lightly beat it to prepare the egg wash. If you don t want to use egg, then you can use only milk. \n 11. Now, take out the prepared dough from the fridge and pat it down on a lightly floured surface. Using a rolling pin, roll it out to the thickness of a chapati/roti. \n 12. You can use dry flour whenever the dough starts sticking to the surface. For easier handling, you can take half of the prepared dough at a time as it will be easier to roll out. \n 13. Using a round utensil, cut out the round shapes from the rolled out dough. I used a 5-inch bowl to cut and it made around 13-14 puffs. \n 14. Now, on half portion of the cut out sheets, first put some grated cheese. Then spread the cooled prepared filling on top of the cheese. Make small cuts on the other half and then fold it over to close the puff. \n 15. Using a fork, press the edges of the puffs to seal them properly. Now, lightly brush the puffs with egg wash/milk wash and sprinkle sesame seeds on top. \n 16. Put the prepared puffs on the baking tray and bake. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve hot and enjoy! \n [EOS]

[BOS] \n **Title:** Thandai Kulfi Recipe - Holi Recipe \n  \n **Cuisine:** Indian | **Diet:** Vegetarian | **Time:** 20 mins prep, 60 mins cook \n  \n **Ingredients:** \n - for the Thandai masala in a mixer grinder \n  \n **Instructions:** \n 1. first we will make a paste of the Thadai Masala by blending all the ingredients for the Thandai masala in a mixer grinder. Keep this thandai masala aside. \n 2. the first step is to have to condense the milk. For this heat milk in a heavy bottomed saucepan and bring it to boil. \n 3. Once the milk comes to a boil, turn the heat to low and simmer the milk with almost continuous stirring and reduce the milk to more than half its quantity. , It is important to note that during the initial stages of milk condensation frequent stirring is important, but as it begins to start condensing and reaches less than half the quantity it is absolutely important that you stir continuously. This is because condensed milk tends to get stuck to the bottom and sides of the pan and burn; leading to a very unpleasant taste. Burning of milk is also toxic so you want to be extra careful. \n 4. Once it the milk is reduced to more than half of its quantity, stir in the sugar until it dissolves completely. Finally stir in the Thandai Paste Mix and give the mixture a good stir. You can even use a , to give it a good whisk. \n 5. Turn off the heat and allow the kulfi mixture to cool completely. Pour the thandai kulfi milk in the moulds until 3/4 th full, seal them airtight and freeze them in the refrigerator. The Thandai Kulfi takes a good fifteen hours or more to freeze. \n 6. Once the Thandai Kulfi is frozen you can run the kulfi moulds under water to enable easy release on to the plate. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve Thandai Kulfi Recipe as a Indian dessert for parties or even make it as a special dessert for the festival of holi. \n [EOS]

Enure the shell does not break. Keep the shell aside. \n 2. Peel the think skin of the pulp, remove any seeds and cut the pulp into tiny pieces and keep this aside. \n 3. The next step is to condense the milk to make the Kulfi. For this heat milk in a heavy bottomed saucepan and bring the milk to a boil. \n 4. Once the milk comes to a boil, turn the heat to low and simmer the milk with almost continuous stirring and reduce the milk to more than half its quantity. , It is important to note that during the initial stages of milk condensation frequent stirring is important, but as it begins to start condensing and reaches less than half the quantity it is absolutely important that you stir continuously. \n 5. This is because condensed milk tends to get stuck to the bottom and sides of the pan and burn; leading to a very unpleasant taste. Burning of milk is also toxic so you want to be extra careful. \n 6. Once it is reduced to about more than half of its quantity stir in the sugar until it dissolves completely. Once it does, allow the kulfi milk mixture to cool completely. \n 7. Once the Kulfi cools, stir in the orange marmalade and the orange pulp mixture into the condensed kulfi mixture. \n 8. Pour the Orange kulfi mixture in the orange shells you kept aside or you can also set in another bowl and later. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** serve the orange kulfi in the orange shells. \n [EOS]

Seal the edges tight and repeat the same process with the remaining dough and make the samosas. \n 12. Heat oil in a , for frying. Once oil turns hot, reduce the flame to medium and drop 2 to 3 samosas at a time and fry until golden brown on all the sides. Drain on absorbent paper. \n 13. Give this delicious and crispy Soya Granule Samosa a try for an evening snack and. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** serve it along with , as an appetizer for Indian Dinner Parties. \n [EOS]

Keep kneading for at least 10 minutes on to a working surface and place it inside the same bowl. \n 4. To make the hummus and Tatziki dip click on the ling and follow the instruction given and keep it ready. \n 9. We will now cook the soaked chickpeas until it is very soft. You will know the chickpeas is cooked well, when you press it between your fingers, it will mash up. \n 11. The next step is to proceed to make the falafel. Combine all the ingredients, including the cooked chickpeas except the oil in a food processor. \n 12. Blend to make a coarse thick paste. Check the salt levels and adjust to suit your taste. Divide the falafel batter into small portions of the size of a ping pong ball and flatten them slightly lightly. \n 13. I use a Kuzhi Paniyaram pan to fry the falafels and the result is very similar to the deep fried ones. \n 14. Add a half a teaspoon of oil into each of the cavities, place the shaped falafel into the cavities and pan fry them until it is crisp and browned on both sides. \n 15. Add few more drops of oil when you flip over to fry them on the other side. This will help in getting the even color for the falafels. \n 16. You can alternatively, heat oil for deep-frying and deep fry these falafels until browned evenly on all sides. Drain them out and place it over napkin to take out the excess oil. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve hot and enjoy! \n [EOS]

[BOS] \n **Title:** Karigadabu Karnataka Style Karanji/ Gujiya recipe \n  \n **Cuisine:** South Indian | **Diet:** Vegetarian | **Time:** 40 mins prep, 50 mins cook \n  \n **Ingredients:** \n - Whole Wheat Flour \n - Sooji (Semolina/ Rava) \n - Rice flour \n - Sunflower Oil \n - Roasted Gram Dal (Pottukadalai) \n - Dessicated Coconut \n - Sugar \n - Cardamom (Elaichi) Pods/Seeds \n  \n **Instructions:** \n 1. To prepare Karigadabu Karnataka Style Karanji recipe, heat ghee in a , . Mix wheat flour, rice flour and semolina in a bowl. Pour hot ghee to this flour and semolina mixture evenly. Ghee bubbles up the flour where it comes in contact with it, so pour in the ghee slowly. \n 2. Mix with fingers after a minute. The mixture will look like bread crumbs. This will ensure you get nice flaky pastry once fried. \n 3. Now add water to knead the pastry dough. Let the dough be stiff and not too soft. Knead it till the pastry dough is smooth. \n 4. Cover the pastry dough with a damp cloth and let it rest till the filling is prepared. \n 5. For the filling, powder fried gram, cardamom, and sugar in a , . To this mixture, add grated coconut and mix well. \n 6. Now remove the damp cloth off the pastry dough. Knead it again for a minute or two, and make small lemon sized balls. \n 7. In a large mixing bowl, sieve out the flour, salt and sugar. Add the cold and cubed unsalted butter into the floor. You can make this dough in the food processor as well. , Work the butter into the flour with your fingers until the mixture resembles a coarse meal. When you hold the flour together, it should hold tight and when you let it loose, it will fall apart. , With a knife, pastry cutter or your hands, cut the butter into the flour. The texture should be as that of coarse breadcrumbs. Don't worry if there are chunks of butter, it ll just make the pastry flakier when it bakes. \n 3. Sprinkle ice water onto the flour and butter mixture. Using your hands push the dough from the sides to the middle of the bowl to form a ball that holds together. Do not knead the dough. \n 4. Make sure to add little water at a time, as the heat from your hands will melt the butter and help form the dough as well. You can transfer the pie dough on to a work surface and knead the dough until all the flour has come together to form a smooth dough. \n 5. Once done, wrap the dough in a cling film or a plastic wrap and refrigerate it for a couple of hours. This refrigeration process helps to give the pie crust a flaky texture. \n 6. As the dough rests, preheat oven to 200 C. \n 7. To make the filling:, Slice the strawberries into 1/4 cm thick slices. Add the caster sugar, cornflour ,and vanilla essence into the strawberry and mix well. \n 8. On a piece of parchment paper, sprinkle some flour, roll out the dough to a circle around 9 to10 inches in size and 1/4 inch thick. \n 9. Add the strawberry filling in the centre, spread the filling at least 2 inches away from the edge of the dough. \n 10. Fold the edges over, or you can also pleat the edges of the dough to make it decorative . Make sure fruit in the centre is still exposed. \n 11. Transfer the parchment to your baking tray. Brush the beaten egg or milk over the dough. \n 12. Sieve some caster sugar over the dough and fruit. Bake for 35 -45 mins at 200 C / 400 F until pastry is golden brown. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve Strawberry Compote Galette along with , to make it a beautiful Sunday lunch. \n [EOS]

[BOS] \n **Title:** Arbi Ajwain Ki Sabzi Recipe (Roasted Colocasia Stir Fry With Ajwain) \n  \n **Cuisine:** Indian | **Diet:** Vegetarian | **Time:** 10 mins prep, 30 mins cook \n  \n **Ingredients:** \n - Colocasia root (Arbi) \n - Ajwain (Carom seeds) \n - Onion \n - Garlic \n - Turmeric powder (Haldi) \n - Red Chilli powder \n - Curry leaves \n - Coriander (Dhania) Leaves \n  \n **Instructions:** \n 1. first wash the arbi well under running water to remove all the dirt and mud. \n 2. Place the arbi in the pressure cooker with quarter cup water. Cover and pressure cook for three to four whistles and turn off the heat. Allow the pressure to release naturally. \n 3. Once done, peel the skin of the arbi and cut it into wedges or dices. Keep aside. \n 4. Heat a teaspoon of oil in a wok/ kadai, add the ajwain seeds, onion and garlic. Saute until the onions become tender. \n 5. Once the onions are tender, add the curry leaves, cooked arbi and the remaining ingredients. Add the salt to taste. \n 6. Stir fry on medium heat for about 3 to 4 minutes until the masalas are well incorporated into the arbi to make a sabzi. Taste and adjust the salt and chili accordingly. \n 7. Once done, remove from the pan, transfer to a serving bowl, stir the coriander leaves and. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** serve. \n [EOS]

[BOS] \n **Title:** Turkish Baklava Recipe From Scratch \n  \n **Cuisine:** Indian | **Diet:** Vegetarian | **Time:** 50 mins prep, 60 mins cook \n  \n **Ingredients:** \n - Vivatta Maida \n - Salt \n - Lemon juice \n - Extra Virgin Olive Oil \n - Lukewarm Water \n - Corn flour \n - Vivatta Maida \n - Pistachios \n - Badam (Almond) \n - Cashew nuts \n - Cinnamon Powder (Dalchini) \n - Butter (unsalted) \n - Sugar \n - Water \n - Honey \n - Cinnamon Stick (Dalchini) \n - Cloves (Laung) \n - Cinnamon Powder (Dalchini) \n - Nutmeg powder \n - Lemon juice \n - Lemon zest \n  \n **Instructions:** \n 1. prepare the homemade phyllo sheet first. , *Making of Phyllo sheet:. \n 2. Mix all purpose flour, salt, olive oil & lemon juice together in a mixing bowl. \n 3. Take warm water and add it to flour mixture gradually until it forms smooth dough. Let it stand for atleast an hour. \n 4. After an hour, divide the dough into two & make about 16 small balls from each & sprinkle some starch mixture over them. \n 5. Take one of the balls & roll it out as thin as you can, with the help of a rolling pin. (My baking tray was of 14 cm circular tray so I rolled out phyllo sheet to completely fit in the baking tray. You can measure it as per your requirement and roll the sheets), Your hand should be visible through the sheet when it is completely rolled out. Sprinkle some starch mixture over it and put it aside covering it with a damp towel. \n 6. Roll out other balls in the same way and put them on the each other sprinkling the starch mixture between their layers. Keep phyllo sheets covered with a damp towel., *Nuts mixture:, Put nuts in a food processor and pulse until they are coarsely grounded. Add sugar and grounded cinnamon to it and mix. Keep aside, *Assembling of Baklava:. \n 7. Preheat the oven at 180 C. Brush baking tray with butter. \n 8. Place 10 phyllo sheets into baking tray one at a time, brushing each sheet with butter. \n 9. Spread 1/3 cup of nuts mixture over layered phyllo sheets. \n 10. Now again place 6 layers of phyllo sheets in to baking tray at a time, brushing each sheet with butter. This time brush it gently or just drizzle butter so that nutty layer doesn t get disturbed. \n 11. Again spread 1/3 cup of nuts mixture and place 6 layers of phyllo sheets applying butter in between the layers. \n 12. Spread 1/3 cup of nuts mixture and place the last 10 layers of phyllo sheets applying butter in between layers. Brush top layer with butter gently. \n 13. Now use a thin & sharp knife to cut it in to square or diamond shape pieces. This step is very important because if you skip it, you can t get perfect pieces once it is baked. \n 14. Bake this in preheated oven at 180 C for 10 minutes and then at 170 C for 20 minutes and at 140 C for 30 minutes. CHeck with your oven settings since each oven differs in its heating capabilities., *Making of Honey syrup:. \n 15. In the meantime when the baklava is baking, make honey syrup. \n 16. Take all the ingredient for honey syrup in a sauce pan & bring it to boil, then let it simmer for 20 30 minutes until it gets soft ball consistenc. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve hot and enjoy! \n [EOS]

In a medium bowl, add the flour and salt. Stir to mix. \n 2. Next, cube the butter and then add it to the flour bowl. Using a pastry blender or two knives, cut the butter into the dough. Using a fork, stir to combine the dough. \n 3. Flour a cutting board, and add the dough. Pat it into a rough square. Flour the rolling pin, and roll the dough out in front of you into a rectangle of approximately about 10 inch. \n 5. Fold the bottom third of the dough over the middle of the dough. Fold the upper third of the dough on top of the middle too. Rotate the dough one-quarter turn, and repeat. Use additional flour as needed to prevent the dough from sticking. \n 6. Roll out, fold, and turn the dough atleast 6 or 7 times. Refrigerate it preferably overnight. \n 7. Remove the dough and roll it in 1/4 inch thin sheet. Cover it generously with sugar. \n 8. Now start rolling the pastry inwards from both corners .cut it 1/4 inch pieces. \n 9. Bake it at 375 F for 15 mins then turn the pastry and bake it for additional 10 min so both the sides are brown and crispy. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve Heart Shaped Sugar Cookies Recipe with a glass of , during evening. \n [EOS]

Heat up 4-5 cup water in a big saucepan. Keep the colander of Amla over it and cover it. Let the amla cool down after steaming. Once it is cooled, remove seed and make small wedges of the cooked amla using a knife. Wear hand gloves while doing so as handling amla for a long time make cause blackening of nails in few cases. \n 4. In a big mixing bowl, first spread the Amla wedges. Now sprinkle the Turmeric powder all over it followed by the Fenugreek powder, Hing , Mustard Seed dal , Salt and Red Chili powder. \n 5. Mix it nicely with a spatula. Now add in the grated Jaggery and mix again. \n 6. Heat up the Oil in a kadai, on a low to medium heat until heated but not fuming. Put off the heat and let the oil cool down a bit. Now add this Oil to the pickle masala and mix very well. Keep the pickle covered overnight. \n 7. Next day oil will float up . Stir it again and fill in clean and dry glass jars. The oil layer should always cover the pickle in the jar. This pickle stays good at room temperature for about 2-3 months. But color may darken slightly, hence you can refrigerate. ,. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve Amla Achaar Recipe , Hot & Sweet Indian Gooseberry Pickle as an accompaniment with , or along with , . \n [EOS]

[BOS] \n **Title:** Milk Braid Rolls Recipe \n  \n **Cuisine:** Indian | **Diet:** Vegetarian | **Time:** 120 mins total \n  \n **Ingredients:** \n - Vivatta Maida \n - Milk \n - Whole Egg \n - Butter (unsalted) \n - Caster Sugar \n - Salt \n - Sugar \n - Vanilla Extract \n - Sesame seeds (Til seeds) \n  \n **Instructions:** \n 1. add all the ingredients to the bowl of stand mixer with dough hook attached. \n 2. Mix all the ingredients on low speed for 2 minutes. Later increase the speed and continue mixing for another ten minutes. \n 3. In case you do not have a stand mixer, take all the ingredients into a bowl and knead them to a dough. The dough would be sticky. \n 4. Later invert the sticky dough on to flat surface and continue kneading for another 15 to 20 minutes until the dough turns out pliable. Do not add any dry flour while kneading once it is off the stand mixer. \n 5. This is time consuming and tricky, but helps in developing the gluten that makes the rolls softer and spongy. \n 6. Do the windowpane test and check for its elasticity and doneness. Windowpane test is done by pulling out a large lemon sized dough and stretching it between the fingers such that the dough is thin, pliable and ready for proofing without getting teared. \n 7. Once the dough is ready, place the kneaded dough in a greased bowl, cover with cling film and set in a warm place until doubled. This might take a couple of hours or more, depending on the temperature of the area. \n 8. Later knock out the air from the dough knead it for a couple of seconds. Weigh your dough and divide into 24 equal portions. \n 9. Roll out each dough portion into logs of 8 to 10 inches long. Take three logs at a time and plait them to a braid, by interlocking one after the other log of dough. \n 10. Repeat the process till done and this recipe plaits 8 braids out of 24 dough portions. You need to divide the dough into logs i multiples of 3. \n 11. Place the braids over baking tray lined with parchment paper. \n 12. Brush them with milk or beaten egg, sprinkle with seeds of choice like sesame, poppy and flax seeds. Cover the tray and set it in a warm place until doubled in size. \n 13. Bake them in a preheated oven at 200 degree celcius for 15 minutes or till done. \n 14. [BOS] \n **Title:** Spicy Lime Pickle Recipe (Naranga Achaar) \n  \n **Cuisine:** Indian | **Diet:** Vegetarian | **Time:** 20 mins prep, 60 mins cook \n  \n **Ingredients:** \n - Lemons \n - Water \n - Salt \n - Garlic \n - Ginger \n - Curry leaves \n - Mustard seeds (Rai/ Kadugu) \n - Methi Seeds (Fenugreek Seeds) \n - Red Chilli powder \n - Turmeric powder (Haldi) \n - Asafoetida (hing) \n - Sesame (Gingelly) Oil \n - Vinegar \n - Salt \n - Jaggery \n  \n **Instructions:** \n 1. in a large sauce pan; bring to boil the whole limes with water and salt. Reduce to medium flame and and simmer for 20 minutes until the lemons are soft. Drain the liquids and allow the lemons to cool. Once cooled cut into small bits (what we did was cut each Lime into 8 quarters, further each quarter into 3-4 pieces). \n 2. In a small bowl, combine the chilli and turmeric powder in a small amount of water to make a paste and keep aside. By mixing masala powder in water, it prevents the powders from burning as soon as they hit the hot pan. \n 3. Heat the oil in a heavy bottomed pan on low heat; add in the mustard seeds and allow it to crackle. Then add in the fenugreek seeds and curry leaves and stir for about a minute. \n 4. Stir in the chopped ginger and garlic and saut for about 10 minutes on medium flame. Add in the powder paste and stir for 4 minutes. Next add in the chopped lemonds and stir well, check for salt and adjust to taste. Finally add in the jaggery and turn off the heat. Stir all the ingredients until well combined. Allow the mixture to cool. \n 5. In a separate pan, add in the vinegar and bring it to a boil. Once cooled stir it into the Spicy Lime Pickle mixture. Transfer to a glass jar and store. You can. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** serve Spicy Lime Pickle Recipe (Naranga Achaar) with , and curd. \n [EOS]

Pour the prepared cake batter into the tray and give a tap to it so that it spreads evenly popping away any air bubbles. \n 9. Bake for about 15 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the center, comes out clean. \n 10. Add instant coffee powder and continue beating till you get stiff peaks. Stop beating at this point. \n 14. Once the cake is cooled, flip it on a greased aluminum foil with smooth side down and spread the whipped cream evenly. \n 15. Gently roll it over starting from one end. \n 16. Wrap the cake with aluminium foil and refrigerate for about an hour. \n 17. Remove the cake from refrigerator and with a knife, cut it into pieces and. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** serve. \n [EOS]

After 4 hours, grind the rice and urad dal to a smooth paste. The batter must be smooth and not grainy. \n 3. You will now mix toddy, yeast, sugar and leave it to ferment for atleast 4 hours which will make the batter to rise well. Make sure you keep this in a warmer place. \n 4. Once the batter is risen well. You can keep your idli steamer on with enough water below to steam. Take a cylindrical shapped vessel or a katori, apply oil and grease well. You can use about as many katoris that can fit in your idli steamer. Traditionally they use a ramkin mould called tondor to do so. \n 5. Mix the risen batter with salt and keep stirring until the salt is evenly distributed. Add the batter carefully inside the katoris or moulds just till the brim. \n 6. Keep these katoris carefully inside the vegetable steamer and steam the sanas for atleast 15 minutes. When you place your finger on the batter after 15 minutes, if it is not found sticky then it is done. \n 7. Switch off the heat, take out the moulds or ramekins and keep it aside to cool down. By using a knife go around the edges and flip the sanas onto a serving plate and do the same for rest. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve the Goan Style Sana Recipe along with , or a , to create make a best brunch for your weekend. \n [EOS]

[BOS] \n **Title:** Aloo Kulcha Recipe (Spiced Potato Stuffed Indian Flat Bread) \n  \n **Cuisine:** North Indian | **Diet:** Vegetarian | **Time:** 15 mins prep, 45 mins cook \n  \n **Ingredients:** \n - All Purpose Flour (Maida) \n - Hung Curd (Greek Yogurt) \n - Baking soda \n - Baking powder \n - Sugar \n - Sunflower Oil \n - Salt \n - Lukewarm Water \n - Potatoes (Aloo) \n - Salt \n - Green Chillies \n - Ginger \n - Chaat Masala Powder \n - Red Chilli powder \n - Cumin powder (Jeera) \n - Coriander Powder (Dhania) \n - Coriander (Dhania) Leaves \n - Ajwain (Carom seeds) \n  \n **Instructions:** \n 1. sieve the all purpose flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt and sugar together to combine them. \n 2. Add the curd and oil to it. Combine it with your fingers. Next add the lukewarm water a little bit at a time while kneading the flour together. Punch, press and pull the dough together kneading it continuously till it forms a firm, but soft dough. \n 3. Knead well for a minimum of 5 to 7 minutes so that the dough is smooth. Apply a little bit of oil all over the dough and cover it with a wet towel. Set it aside in a warm place for 3 to 4 hours to rise a little bit. You can do this in a just-warmed oven, if you live in a cold place. \n 4. In the meantime, prepare the stuffing for the kulcha. Mash the boiled and peeled potatoes, in a mixing bowl. \n 5. Add salt, green chillies, coriander powder, cumin powder, grated ginger, chat masala, red chilli powder, garam masala, coriander leaves and mix well with your fingers till it is a evenly combined potato mixture. \n 6. Now, to prepare the Aloo Kulchas, turn out the dough onto a work surface dusted with a little flour. Knead it for 3-4 minutes, then roll out the dough into a long cylinder and cut it into 8 individual portions. \n 7. Rolle acc of the portions into a ball. Taking one ball at a time, flatten it out with your fingers to form a small disc about 3 inches in diameter. Take a spoonful of the spicy potato filling, place it in the centre of the disc. \n 8. Bring the edges of the dic together into the centre and seal the filling inside to make a stuffed dough ball. \n 9. Flatten it down slightly with your palm, and using a little flour for dusting, roll it out gently with a rolling pin to make a thin round about 5 inches in diameter. The kulcha will be slightly thicker than a usual chapati due to the stuffing. Take care not to let the stuffing ooze out of the kulcha. \n 10. Next, wet your palms with a little water and pat one side of the kulcha with it. Sprinkle a pinch of ajwain seeds and chopped coriander leaves over it and press down so they stick to the kulcha. \n 11. Warm a skillet or tava on a medium heat. When it is hot enough, place the kulcha on it, wet side down. \n 12. Now, wet your palms again and pat the other side as the kulcha cooks on a medium heat. [BOS] \n **Title:** Mithi Mathri Recipe (Crispy Fried Sweet Fritters) \n  \n **Cuisine:** Indian | **Diet:** Vegetarian | **Time:** 30 mins prep, 45 mins cook \n  \n **Ingredients:** \n - All Purpose Flour (Maida) \n - Chiroti Rava \n - Salt \n - Lukewarm Water \n - Water \n - Sugar \n - Cardamom Powder (Elaichi) \n  \n **Instructions:** \n 1. Mithi Mathri Recipe, first lets prepare the dough. Mix the maida, sooji and salt together in a mixing bowl. \n 2. Next, add the ghee to the mixture and rub between your fingers until the dough turns crumbly and resembles breadcrumbs. \n 3. Add the warm water to it a little by little, while bringing it together into a dough. Press together till it forms a ball. Knead the dough for 3-4 minutes till it no longer sticks, and easily forms a ball. Set it aside to rest for 5 minutes. Then, knead it again till soft for about 5 minutes. \n 4. Cover the dough with a muslin cloth and let it rest for 30 minutes. \n 5. After 30 minutes, divide the dough in 16 equal parts. Make balls and keep aside for 5 minutes, Next, roll out the mathris by rolling each ball into a disc, about 1/4 inch thick and 2-3 inches in diameter. Poke the rolled out mathri with fork or knife so that it doesn't fluff up while frying. \n 6. Warm some oil in a kadhai and deep fry the mathris for 2-3 minutes on each side until they turn golden brown. Remove from the oil using a slotted spoon and keep aside to cool. \n 7. Meanwhile, prepare the sugar syrup by boiling together water, sugar and cardamom powder in a heavy-bottomed saucepan. \n 8. Once the mixture comes to a boil, reduce the heat and continue to cook till the syrup reaches two-string consistency. This should take about 8-10 minutes on low heat. \n 9. Switch off the heat and dip the pre-fried mathri in to the sugar syrup. Keep the mathri sub-merged in sugar syrup for about 30 seconds so that it is completely coated. \n 10. Place the sugar-coated mathri on a tray till completely dry. Then the Mithi Mathri store in an airtight container when completely dry and cool. You can make this ahead and. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** serve it at a festive gathering too. \n [EOS]

[BOS] \n **Title:** Maharashtrian Dinkache Ladoo Recipe (Whole Wheat Flour Truffles With Edible Gum & Dry Fruits) \n  \n **Cuisine:** Indian | **Diet:** Vegetarian | **Time:** 30 mins total \n  \n **Ingredients:** \n - Whole Wheat Flour \n - White Urad Dal (Split) \n - Dessicated Coconut \n - Dry dates powder (kharik pud) \n - Sugar \n - Mixed nuts \n - Gond (natural gum) \n - Cardamom Powder (Elaichi) \n - Nutmeg powder \n - Dry ginger powder \n  \n **Instructions:** \n 1. heat a heavy bottom pan and dry roast the split and skinned black gram on a low to medium flame for 7-10 minutes. \n 2. Keep stirring the dal to ensure it is been roasted evenly and it does not catch the bottom of the pan. You will get a nice aroma while you roast the dal. Remove the roasted dal in a plate. On cooling, grind to a fine powder using a grinder. , Grate the dry coconut using grater and keep aside. Take edible gum in a grinder jar and make a fine powder. Similarly powder the sugar and keep aside. \n 3. Dry roast the dry fruits on low to medium flame for about 3- 5 minutes. On cooling coarsely grind them or chop them. \n 4. Heat the same heavy bottom large wok , add 1/2 cup ghee and to it add the powdered urad dal .Fry on low flame until pink in color. This may take around 5 minutes. \n 5. Now add the whole wheat flour to the roasted urad dal in batches and keep stirring continuously. Roast the wheat flour for about 4-5 minutes without adding more ghee. \n 6. To the roasted urad dal and wheat flour, add the powdered edible gum. Roast for 2-3 minutes. \n 7. Now add the powdered dried dates. Roast for 1-2 minutes.(In many Indian groceries, you can get powdered dry dates easily . In case you do not find, it can be made at home. De seed the dried dates ( chuara/ Kharik ) . Now cut into small pieces using a sharp knife or scissors. Put the chopped pieces of dried dates into a grinder jar or food processor to get a coarse powder ). \n 8. Now add grated dried coconut followed by the chopped nuts to the mixture and keep stirring the entire mixture using a large ladle. \n 9. Now put off the heat and add the powdered sugar followed by the dry ginger powder and the sweet masala. Blend everything very well. If not making the ladoos as offering to God, you can taste the ladoo mixture at this stage. \n 10. Now our ladoo mixture is ready. Add the remaining melted 1/2 cup ghee to it as needed. Mix well and check by taking handful of mixture in your palms, if you are able to bind ladoos, do not add more ghee. If you are not able to form a ball shape then you can add all the remaining ghee. Roll between the palm to give a round shape. \n 11. Make all the ladoos similarly while still warm. As once the mixture cools down, then the ghee solidifies making it difficult to bind the ladoos. This happens especially in the area where the temperature is low. , On cooling keep the ladoos in air tight containers and store at room temper. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve hot and enjoy! \n [EOS]

Turn off the heat and let the curdled milk rest for 3-4 minutes in its whey. \n 3. After about 3 to 4 minutes, strain the curdled milk onto a cheesecloth or a cloth strainer. Let it drip and drain until all the whey has drained out and we have thick cottage cheese (chenna). This will take a few hours. So proceed to the next steps once the chenna is ready. \n 4. Meanwhile, heat the remaining 1 liter milk in a heavy bottom pan and cook on medium heat till the milk has reduced to half. Keep stirring the milk occasionally to prevent the milk from getting settled at the bottom of the pan. \n 5. Once the milk has reduced to half its quantity, add the 1/2 cup sugar, a pinch of orange color and orange essence to the reduced milk and keep this aside. Pour the reduced milk into a serving bowl which is large enough to hold the cooked chenna balls. \n 6. Once the chenna is ready, we will proceed to shape the chenna. Place the chenna into a bowl, add arrowroot powder and a pinch of orange color to it. Mash the chenna with the heels of your palm till smooth. The process is more like a kneading and mash technique that makes the chenna soft. Continue with the knead and mash motion until the chenna feels soft. \n 7. Once the chenna is soft, shape the chenna into 12 to 15 small balls and flatten them slightly. Keep these balls aside. \n 8. The next step is to cook the chenna - yes its double cooking process to get the spongy nature of the cottage cheese balls in the Ras Malai. \n 9. To begin, heat water and 1-1/2 cup sugar in a pressure cooker. Stir well until all the sugar has dissolved completely. When the water comes to a rolling boil, add a few chenna balls in the pressure cooker. Cover the lid, place the weight on and cook the chenna balls for 2 whistles on high heat.Remove the pressure cooker. \n 10. After the two whistles, turn off the heat, place the pressure cooker under running water to release the pressure immediately. The process of placing the pressure cooker under cold water ensures safety when releasing the pressure. \n 11. Once you open, you will notice the Chenna Balls would have puffed up and expanded. Remove the cooked chenna balls using a slotted spoon and add them to the reduced milk. \n 12. Cook the remaining chenna balls in the same manner and add them to the reduced milk. The Orange Rasmalai is now ready to be refrigerated. \n 13. Place the Orange Rasmalai in. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve hot and enjoy! \n [EOS]

Cut them into halves and keep aside. \n 2. Peel the potato and chop it into small pieces and keep it in a bowl of water until it is needed. Setting chopped potatoes aside in water helps retain their colour. \n 3. Next, prepare the mustard paste. Place all the ingredients listed under for mustard paste into a blender and grind to a fine but thick paste. Add as little water as possible in order to ensure that the paste is thick and not runny. \n 4. Now, to begin making the curry, add about 2 tablespoons of oil into a kadai or a heavy bottomed pan on a medium heat. \n 5. First add the potatoes, sprinkle some salt and saute until they are almost cooked and get a light brown colour. Once the potatoes are cooked, transfer them to a paper towel to drain the excess oil and keep aside. \n 6. In the same kadai, add the chopped tomatoes and toss them for a minute. Next, add the chopped mushrooms. Saute these on high heat for 6-8 minutes, until the mushrooms are half cooked. Add the roasted potatoes and turmeric powder and toss together for another couple of minutes. \n 7. To this, add the prepared mustard paste, mix well and saute for 2 more minutes. Add salt and required amount of water of the gravy, as per the consistency you desire. Allow the curry to come to a boil so the masalas get cooked thoroughly. Simmer the Odia Chatu Besara on low to medium heat for about 5 minutes, until all the masalas get well absorbed by the vegetables. \n 8. Garnish with chopped coriander leaves and. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** serve the Odia Chatu Besara along with dinner. \n [EOS]

To begin making the Spicy Tandoori Paneer Open Puff Recipe by making the butter log first. Use the unsalted butter which hard and cut them into small cubes. \n 2. Spread them on a cling film and wrap it in such a way the u can roll it flat. Using rolling pin roll the butter into a rectangular shape about 2 centimeter thick. Make sure u do this quickly otherwise the butter will melt quickly. \n 3. Place the rolled butter in the cling film itself and keep it in the refrigerator for 15 minutes. \n 4. In the meanwhile make the dough, add all the ingredients in a mixing bowl. Using your hand create a crumble texture with the dough by mixing the flour and butter together. \n 5. Slowly add water and knead it into a soft dough, keep it in the refrigerator for 10 minutes. Once done take out the dough and start rolling it into a rectangular shape so you can wrap the rectangular butter log with this dough. \n 6. Once it is rolled, take out the butter and place it in the center, fold in and wrap the butter inside make sure you seal all openings by just pinching the dough. \n 7. After sealing, gently roll the dough keeping the rectangular shape intact. Keep dusting flour on the dough and rolling it so that it does not stick. Keep edges straight and even. Don t overwork the dough. \n 8. Roll it into a long rectangular shape about 20 cm length to 10 cm breadth, keep the long length facing towards you, fold the left side to the middle and the right side as well, so that the two edges meet the center. \n 9. Now fold it like a book and dust some more flour and refrigerate by covering it with a cling film for 10 minutes.Repeat the process around 5 times, make sure you refrigerate the dough every time you do the book folding. \n 10. Keep the edges straight and do not over work it.In the meanwhile, pre-heat the oven to 220 degrees Celsius and keep it ready for baking. \n 11. Heat a sauce pan with oil, add onions, ginger and garlic paste and saute until the onions soften. \n 12. Add tomatoes and the spice powders and saute well till the tomatoes are cooked. Mash them well as you cook. \n 13. Add bell peppers, crumbled paneer, sweet corn and mix well, at the end add curd and give it a nice mix. Saute until the masala has combined well. \n 14. Take the dough out, roll it into a rectangle with 2 centimeter thickness. Cut the big rectangle into small squares about 10 centimeter. \n 15. Take a heap tablespoon of the filling and place them in the center of each square. Place these puffs over a greased tray. \n 16. Brush them with olive oil and sprinkle some toasted sesame seeds and bake in the ov. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve hot and enjoy! \n [EOS]

[BOS] \n **Title:** Chettinad Style Puliyogare Gojju Recipe \n  \n **Cuisine:** Indian | **Diet:** Vegetarian | **Time:** 20 mins prep, 30 mins cook \n  \n **Ingredients:** \n - Dry Red Chillies \n - Whole Black Peppercorns \n - Cumin seeds (Jeera) \n - Chana dal (Bengal Gram Dal) \n - White Urad Dal (Split) \n - Sesame seeds (Til seeds) \n - Dry coconut (kopra) \n - Mustard seeds \n - Curry leaves \n - Asafoetida (hing) \n - Jaggery \n - Roasted Peanuts (Moongphali) \n - Sunflower Oil \n  \n **Instructions:** \n 1. get prep with all the ingredients mentioned and keep them handy. \n 2. In a kadai, dry roast each of the ingredients individually one at a time, on a low heat - Urad Dal, Chana Dal - both until slightly brown, black pepper, Cumin seeds, Red Chillies a bit until fragrant. \n 3. Allow to cool by spreading them on a large plate. Once cooled, grind all the above dry roasted ingredients by using a mixer grinder. Set aside. \n 4. Next dry roast these ingredients: Sesame seeds, Dry coconut. Coarsely grind both of these ingredients and mix it with the ground spices you prepared in mixer earlier. \n 5. In an aluminium vessel, or a thick bottomed Kadai, heat about 2 cups of water, add jaggery, tamarind pulp, salt to taste and bring to a boil. Check on the tangy v/s sweet admixture of flavours. Adjust as per requirement by adding in more jaggery/tamarind pulp - as this is the mixture that gives the rice its unique flavour. \n 6. Allow to cool. Once the jaggery - tamarind mixture cools down add the ground dal spice & coconut powder and stir well to form a nice thick semi dry dough like consistency. Set aside. \n 7. [BOS] \n **Title:** Kadali Bhanda O Chingudi Tarkari Recipe (Odia Style Banana Blossom & Prawn Curry) \n  \n **Cuisine:** Oriya | **Diet:** Non-Vegetarian | **Time:** 40 mins prep, 25 mins cook \n  \n **Ingredients:** \n - Banana flower (Vazhaipoo) \n - Prawns \n - Potato (Aloo) \n - Onion \n - Bay leaf (tej patta) \n - Cinnamon Stick (Dalchini) \n - Cardamom (Elaichi) Pods/Seeds \n - Cloves (Laung) \n - Dry Red Chillies \n - Cumin seeds (Jeera) \n - Cumin powder (Jeera) \n - Sugar \n - Turmeric powder (Haldi) \n - Red Chilli powder \n - Mustard oil \n - Salt \n - Fresh coconut \n  \n **Instructions:** \n 1. Take a kitchen towel and spread it on your kitchen platform. Rub both of your palms with mustard oil before preparing this banana blossom. Take a bowl aside with water and squeeze a lemon into it. \n 2. Now peel and discard the purple covers of the blossom, then gently remove the outer skin of each of the florets and take out the thin stem from the floret. The skin and the stems are not consumed, hence thrown away. \n 3. Once done, soak all the florets in cold water with lemon juice for half an hour, so as to prevent them from turning dark and bitter. \n 4. Now pressure cook these banana blossom with salt and turmeric till cooked and then discard the water. Now banana blossom is ready for cooking. \n 5. Clean and devein the prawns. Apply salt and turmeric powder to the prawns and keep aside for 10 minutes. \n 6. Peel and cube the potato and finely slice the onion. \n 7. Heat oil in a pan. shallow fry the cubed potatoes till nicely golden from all sides. Take out and keep aside. \n 8. In the same pan, shallow fry the prawns over high heat for 2 mins on both sides, take out and keep aside. \n 9. Heat more oil in the pan. \n 10. Now add whole garam masala (cinnamon sticks, green cardamom, cloves), bay leaf, cumin seeds, dry red chilies to the oil. Cook on medium heat till the masala releases nice flavor. \n 11. [BOS] \n **Title:** Homemade Tamarind Paste Recipe \n  \n **Cuisine:** Indian | **Diet:** Vegetarian | **Time:** 90 mins prep, 17 mins cook \n  \n **Ingredients:** \n - Tamarind \n - Water \n  \n **Instructions:** \n 1. heat about 2-3 cups of water in a saucepan. Make sure that water should be hot enough and not just warm. \n 2. Add Tamarind in 1-1/2 cup hot water and keep rest of the water aside(we'll be needing that later), keep it aside for an hour or till tamarind turns soft. \n 3. Squeeze off the tamarind well. \n 4. Pass the squeezed tamarind through a strainer to a heavy bottomed pan. \n 5. Discard the seeds and rest of the discard which is left over in strainer. \n 6. Add the pulp back to the first pot in which we added tamarind and water.Now do the same process,add water to the tamarind pulp. \n 7. Keep it aside for 10 minutes, squeeze it again and pass it through strainer. \n 8. Now you'll find thick paste. (If not then you can repeat same process one more time). \n 9. Boil the paste on a medium heat for 4-5 minutes but make sure that it does not get burnt, keep stirring it in between., turn off the flame and cool the tamarind paste down and store it in a glass jar and refrigerate. \n 10. Homemade Tamarind Paste Recipe can stay good for a month in a glass jar. Make sure that the jar is airtight and use a clean and dry spoon every time you use the paste. You can use the tamarind paste as and when required. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve hot and enjoy! \n [EOS]

Add one tablespoon of oil to coat the dough and knead again. Cover and set aside for 15 minutes. \n 3. Knead once again and divide the dough into 8 portions. Preheat the iron skillet on medium heat. \n 4. Roll the paratha dough portions into balls and flatten them with the palm of your hand. Toss them on flour and roll them out into circles of approximately 3 inches in diameter. Put 1/4 teaspoon oil and spread it on the rolled dough. \n 5. We need to get a triangle shape, to do so, first fold into a semi-circle, then fold the semi-circle into half again. You get a mini triangle shape. Tossing the triangle on a little flour, roll it out gently into a larger triangle. Continue the same process of rolling with the remaining dough portions. \n 6. With skillet on medium high heat, place one rolled out dough on the skillet. After a few seconds you will notice an air pockets popping out. At this point flip the plain paratha and smear about 1/2 a teaspoon of ghee. Using a flat spatula do a light pressing and turning motion to cook to the pudhina paratha. \n 7. Flip to the other side and press and turn in a similar way. You will notice brown spots around the pudhina parathas and it will be slightly crisp. Remove from heat and place on a platter or. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** serve hot. \n [EOS]

The Athirasa can now be stored in an air tight container and eaten either immediately or even during the week. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve Adhirasam/Athirasam Recipe (A Traditional South Indian Diwali Sweet) for a snack along with , during evenings. \n [EOS]

Saute for a couple of seconds. \n 19. Now turn off the flame and add jeera powder, dhaniya powder, red chili powder, fennel powder and black pepper powder. Mix well. Turn on the flame and saute for 1-2 minutes on a low flame so that spice powders does not burn. \n 20. Add spinach puree and cook for about 2-3 minutes. \n 21. [BOS] \n **Title:** Instant Lemon Pickle Recipe \n  \n **Cuisine:** Indian | **Diet:** Vegetarian | **Time:** 10 mins prep, 30 mins cook \n  \n **Ingredients:** \n - Lemons \n - Sugar \n - Salt \n - Red Chilli powder \n  \n **Instructions:** \n 1. Cut each lemon into 8 pieces. Remove the seeds using a knife. Make sure no seeds are left inside the lemon pieces as it may lend a bitter taste to the pickle. \n 3. Add 3-4 cups of water in a pressure cooker. Keep all the lemon pieces in a vessel and place the vessel in the cooker. Cover the vessel with a plate so that water from steam doesn t fall in it. \n 4. Pressure cook the lemons for 1 whistle and then lower the flame and allow to cook for another 10-12 minutes. , Open the cooker once the pressure has released. You will see the lemon pieces are cooked well and the juice has accumulated. \n 5. Strain the lemon pieces and collect the juice in a pan. , Do not add any water to it. Add sugar to the lemon juice and cook on low flame. \n 6. Keep stirring. The sugar will melt and you will get the syrup. Cook the syrup until all the sugar has dissolved and you see bubbles in the syrup. , The syrup attains a 2 string consistency by this stage. As the juice is very less and we do not add any extra water, this stage attains very fast say in about 5-7 minutes. \n 7. Add salt and red chili powder to the syrup and stir well. At the end add the cooked lemon pieces and put off the flame. Mix the pieces well with the sauce. Keep stirring the pickle for 1-2 minutes. \n 8. The Instant Lemon Pickle Recipe is ready. Let it cool down completely. Transfer to clean dry and sterilized bottle and refrigerate. Use Instant Lemon Pickle Recipe as per need. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve hot and enjoy! \n [EOS]

[BOS] \n **Title:** Andi Unda (Kerala Special Cashew & Rice Balls) Recipe \n  \n **Cuisine:** Kerala | **Diet:** Vegetarian | **Time:** 10 mins prep, 30 mins cook \n  \n **Ingredients:** \n - Red matta rice \n - Cashew nuts \n - Jaggery \n - Dry coconut (kopra) \n  \n **Instructions:** \n 1. roast the red matta rice in a , without oil. The rice will become crispy and starts crackling. Once you start hearing the sound of crackle, take it off the stove and let it cool on a flat plate. \n 2. In the same , , add the cashew-nuts and dry roast them until they turn brown. Take care not to burn or black them. Once roasted, spread them on a flat plate to cool down. \n 3. In a , , first, grind the rice to a fine powder. Next grind the cashew-nuts. Do not run the mixer continuously, it will result in cashew butter, we don't need cashew paste, we need powdered cashews, so just pulse it 4-5 times. \n 4. Mix powdered cashews, powdered rice, powdered jaggery and coconut together. Transfer the mixture to a , and pulse them together 4-5 times to mix it well. This will help to bind them easily into balls. \n 5. Transfer the contents to a clean bowl, take fist pull of powder and start making balls by pressing it tightly in your palms, shaping them like laddus. Keep the balls in a clean flat plate. Follow the same process with the remaining mixture. \n 6. Andi Unda tastes best within 2-3 days. If you are planning to store for more days, then keep them in an air-tight container in the refrigerator. But then too, it is best to consume them within a week or 10 days. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve them as a snack during hunger-pangs or even as a regular addition to your kids lunch box to improve their nutrient intake. \n [EOS]

After the poppy seeds cool down grind them into powder. \n 6. The satori should puff up, when you fry them. \n 9. Keep the satori to cool on a kitchen towel, you can store them upto 7 to 10 days in an airtight box. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve Satori as a sweet side dish for the festivals along with your festive meal. \n [EOS]

Set aside for at least 2 hrs or more in a refrigerator, For the gravy masala : In a small wok/kadai - heat 1 tbsp ghee/butter (not oil) and fry the almonds for 3-4 mins on low flame.Strain the almonds off excess ghee, cool them and grind to a fine paste by adding just about 200 ml of water. Set aside. \n 3. In the same pan, with left over ghee/melted butter, fry the chopped onions until golden brown. Once cool, blend it into a fine paste & set aside. (you should have about 1 cup). \n 4. Heat a nice big chunk of ghee/butter in a grill girdle (or you can bake the ribs in an OTG @ 140 c for 15-20 mins). I used a grill girdle, since it gives me more control in evenly browning the pieces and checking if the meat is well done with full freedom - which an oven lacks, since you cant keep opening it every now & then. \n 5. Place the meat pieces on a well heated grill girdle. Ensure you spread the marinade liquid over the ribs and don't throw it away. \n 6. Cook until you notice the outer layer getting caramelised and the meat is well done. Keep adding additional butter/brush the meat pieces with butter if you notice them sticking to the pan.Once done - Set the pieces aside and collect the leftover melted butter/ghee marinade mixture in a small bowl (which will pretty much be like a buttery brown sauce). \n 7. In a deep, non stick pan melt 2 tablespoons butter/ghee. \n 8. Add in the whole spices mentioned under Sauce Ingredients - let them splutter and induce their fragrance into the butter/ghee. \n 9. Add in the fried onion paste, ginger paste and garlic paste. \n 10. Cook this onion/ginger/garlic mixture until all the water evaporates, it should turn slightly brown and oil starts to separate. \n 11. Next add in the ground almond paste - turn down the flame to medium. \n 12. Ensure that you are constantly stirring to avoid any sticking/burning at the bottom of the pan. Cook until all the water evaporates - leaving a thick consistency behind. Be careful not to burn or overly brown the sauce base. \n 13. Add in the Red chilli powder basis the spice levels desired and stir well. \n 14. Add one cup of water and bring the mixture to a boil. Once it starts boiling add the marinade -ghee sauce mixture (collected after grilling the ribs) and stir. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve hot and enjoy! \n [EOS]

To prepare Tamil Nadu Style Milagu Thattai Recipe (Peppered dal-rice fritters), in a medium size bowl, add the sieved rice and the urad dal flour. \n 2. Add salt, asafoetida, sesame seeds, pepper powder, chana dal, curry leaves and mix all the dry ingredients. \n 3. Now add butter and rub it into the flour. \n 4. Add hot oil and add water little by little to form a smooth, crack free dough. \n 5. Cover the bowl with a damp cloth and allow the dough to rest for 30 minutes. \n 6. After the resting time, take small portions of the dough in greased hands, roll it into a smooth crack free ball. While shaping the thattai, keep the remaining dough covered with moist cloth to prevent the dough from drying. \n 7. Place the dough ball on a dry kitchen towel or butter paper and flatten it into thin roundels. \n 8. Heat oil in a , . Test the heat of oil by dropping a small portion of dough, if its rises to top immediately, that indicates the oil is hot. \n 9. Fry the milagu thattai over low/medium flame till the sizzling sound stops and the thattai is uniformly browned. Overheated oil does not help in even cooking, hence cook on medium flame. \n 10. Repeat this process for the entire batch. \n 11. Once cooled, store them in a clean, odour free air tight container. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve Tamil Nadu Style Milagu Thattai Recipe (Peppered dal-rice fritters) with filter coffee on a rainy day. \n [EOS]

Fry till the color of the crepe/utanki is golden brown and then remove the crepe on to a kitchen towel, with the help of a perforated ladle, draining the excess oil back into the deep frying pan. Roll them up with the help of a rolling pin immediately, such that they harden in that shape when cooled. \n 8. Once oil is hot enough add the chopped garlic and grated ginger. Stir fry on low heat till garlic turns light brown in color. \n 4. Add the soaked moong dal along with turmeric powder, red chili powder, mango powder and 2 cups of water and stir to combine. Close the lid of the pressure cooker and let the moong dal cook over medium heat for 2 to 3 whistles. Turn off the heat. Allow the pressure to release naturally. \n 5. While the dal is cooking in the pressure cooker, in a pan heat a teaspoon of oil over medium heat. Add the chopped radish greens and cook until the greens are wilted and cooked through. Turn off the heat and keep aside. \n 6. Once the pressure has released, open the lid of the pressure cooker and gently mash the dal with the back of the spoon. This will help thicken the moong dal. Add the cooked radish greens and stir to combine. Check the salt and spice levels and adjust to suit your taste. \n 7. The last step is to temper the dal. In a tadka pan, heat some ghee on medium heat. When it is warm, add the cumin seeds. Once they crackle, add the red chilli, roast the chillies for a few seconds and turn off the heat. \n 8. Pour the tadka over the dal and stir to combine. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve Moong Dal With Radish Greens hot along with accompaniments rice and salad. \n [EOS]

[BOS] \n **Title:** How to Cook Root Vegetables like Potatoes using a Pressure Cooker \n  \n **Cuisine:** Indian | **Diet:** Vegetarian | **Time:** 2 mins total \n  \n **Ingredients:** \n - Potatoes \n - Water \n  \n **Instructions:** \n 1. To begin pressure cooking the potatoes, first thoroughly clean them under running water. You can lightly scrub them too, to remove all the excess oil and grime that is usually present on the peels of potatoes and other underground spuds. \n 2. Next, you can either cut the potatoes into half or place the whole potato into the pressure cooker. \n 3. Add 1/4 cup of water into the cooker. Place the lid over it along with the weight. Cover and cook on a high heat until you hear the about two whistles. \n 4. After the first two whistles, turn the heat to low and simmer for three minutes, after which you can turn the heat off. \n 5. Once you turn the heat off, wait for the pressure to release naturally as the steam present inside continues to cook the potatoes for a while longer. This may take up to 10 minutes. Once the pressure has released, you will be able to lift the weight easily and open the lid of the cooker. \n 6. You can test the potatoes for done-ness by inserting a knife into them. If the knife passes in easily, the potatoes are cooked. Cool them completely to make peeling them easier for you. \n 7. Once peeled, you can either use as is, or mash them up for recipes like , or other even other spuds like Arbi/Colocasia used in , or yams, as used in this , . \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve hot and enjoy! \n [EOS]

Now add the tamarind extract, enough salt and the fried ginger, and mix well. Allow this to come to a boil. \n 9. Add the powdered jaggery and cook till the mixture thickens a little. Inji Curry has to be refrigerated because it uses onions. So store in an airtight container and place in refrigerator., 2. Inji Curry always tastes better if made ahead. As it sits, the flavors are enhanced. So once the curry is prepared, allow it to sit for a few hours before consuming or storing in the refrigerator. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve hot and enjoy! \n [EOS]

[BOS] \n **Title:** How to Make Tutty Fruity Recipe \n  \n **Cuisine:** Continental | **Diet:** Vegetarian | **Time:** 20 mins prep, 60 mins cook \n  \n **Ingredients:** \n - Raw papaya \n - Sugar \n - Vanilla Extract \n - Saffron strands \n  \n **Instructions:** \n 1. To make Tutti Fruity, get the papaya washed, peel, remove its seeds and chop it finely. \n 2. Blanch the papaya in boiling water for 3 minutes, switch off heat and let the pieces soak for another 5 minutes. \n 3. Drain the chopped papayas after soaking. \n 4. Dissolve sugar in 2 cups of water and stir on medium heat until sugar dissolves completely. \n 5. Add papaya pieces in sugar syrup. \n 6. Now cook until sugar syrup gets to one thread consistency, and until sugar syrup become viscous and papaya pieces are cooked completely. \n 7. Turn off heat and add 1 tsp of vanilla essence in syrup. \n 8. Add saffron for natural color. You can also add food color if you want. Divide the mixture, put in separate bowls to add various colors. Let these papaya pieces absorb the color and sugar syrup for next 16-24 hours. Cover and keep aside. Toss for every few hours for the color to be even. \n 9. After the soaking time, take out the papayas and place them on a wire net placed on top of a plate. This is to drain out any extra syrup and dry the pieces and be freed of stickiness completely. This process speeds up under the sun. It may take 2-3 days depending on the temperature, humidity and the sunlight. \n 10. After that, you can store the Tutti Fruity Recipe in an airtight container and use it whenever you want. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve hot for best results. \n [EOS]

[BOS] \n **Title:** How To Cook Legumes in a Pressure Cooker & Sauce Pan \n  \n **Cuisine:** Indian | **Diet:** Vegetarian | **Time:** 10 mins prep, 40 mins cook \n  \n **Ingredients:** \n - Kabuli Chana (White Chickpeas) \n - Water \n - Salt \n  \n **Instructions:** \n 1. Heavier pulses like chickpea, kidney beans, and the like; soak them in water completely immersed for a minimum of 8 hours before they can be pressure cooked (one cup of pulse to 3 cups of water). Drain the water that it was soaked in. \n 2. To begin cooking the legumes in the pressure cooker method, place the soaked pulse along with 3 cups of fresh water in the pressure cooker with its whistle on. \n 3. Allow the whistle to blow 5-6 times on medium high heat; turn the heat to low and simmer for another 20 to 30 minutes before you can turn off. \n 4. Wait for the pressure to release completely before opening. \n 5. Note: The cooking process continues in the pressure cooker even when the heat is turned off. \n 6. To begin cooking the legumes in a sauce pan, drain the water they have been soaked in, rinse the beans thoroughly, and cook with three cups of fresh water. \n 7. Bring the beans to boil uncovered for about ten minutes. After about 10 minutes of boiling, you will notice some foam collected, you can choose to skim it off or leave it in. \n 8. Turn the heat to low and simmer for about half an hour to 45 minutes until the beans are tender. After the first half hour stir in the salt and simmer until tender and cooked. \n 9. Stirring in the salt earlier can take the beans longer to cook. \n 10. Stir every 15 minutes adding more water as and when needed. When ready turn off heat, allow it to sit covered for about 10 minutes and it will be ready to use. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve hot and enjoy! \n [EOS]

Pick a kadai and boil the dates with chopped pineapples in a cup of water for 5 minutes on medium flame. \n 2. Switch off the flame and add salted butter. Let the mixture cool down completely. \n 3. Once cooled, add the mix to mixer grinder and make a fine puree. \n 4. In a big mixing bowl, beat the eggs with an electric beater on high for about 2 minutes. \n 5. Add vanilla essence and fold in. \n 6. Sift flour and baking soda in egg mixture bit by bit and intermittently mixing with a spatula. \n 7. Add in the prepared pineapple dates puree and mix well with the spatula. Make sure that there are no lumps. \n 8. Mix in raisins in this batter. \n 9. Grease a loaf pan with oil and pour this batter in it. \n 10. Bake at 375 degree Fahrenheit preheated oven for approximately 30 minutes. (Baking time may vary upon individual oven). Check if the cake is done with the help of a toothpick. If it comes out clean after inserting in the middle of the cake, that means your cake is done, else, keep it for a longer period of time. This cake takes comparatively little longer to bake than cakes without fruits in its ingredients. \n 11. Remove and keep it on the cooling rack for 15 minutes or until cooled to room temperature. \n 12. Flip the cake onto a plate, cut and enjoy your guilt free Sugarless Pineapple Dates Cake. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve hot and enjoy! \n [EOS]

[BOS] \n **Title:** Mango Panna Cotta With Fruit Cream Recipe \n  \n **Cuisine:** Indian | **Diet:** Vegetarian | **Time:** 20 mins prep, 120 mins cook \n  \n **Ingredients:** \n - Double Cream \n - Milk \n - Agar agar \n - Sugar \n - Heavy whipping cream \n - Mixed fruits \n  \n **Instructions:** \n 1. To prepare mango panna cotta with fruit cream recipe, you have to start first by chopping the agar-agar strands into small pieces with the help of kitchen scissors and soak them in warm water for about 10 minutes. \n 2. Mix cream, milk, and sugar in a pan or saucepan and keep it on low flame. Keep on stirring at intervals while the cream mixture comes to a gentle boil and sugar gets completely dissolved. \n 3. Meanwhile, keep the agar-agar and water solution on low flame in another saucepan. Keep on stirring the agar-agar solution and let it cook till the agar-agar strands are dissolved. \n 4. When the cream, milk, and sugar mixture comes to a gentle boil, switch off the flame, and mix hot agar-agar solution with it and stir very well with a wired whisk. \n 5. Cook this mixture on low flame for about 5 minutes. At any point of time mixture should not come to a rolling boil; rather should be at a constant boil. Switch off the flame. \n 6. Peel and chop the mangoes and then make a smooth puree of the mangoes in a ,. \n 7. After about 10 minutes of keeping the milk and agar mixture off the fire, when it cools down a little, add the Mango puree. \n 8. Mix it well with the help of a wire whisk. The mixture should be smooth. \n 9. Now, pour this prepared warm Panna Cotta either into individual glasses/bowls or in any convenient dish/glass dish. You can tilt the glasses to have unique patterns or can set it in individual molds. \n 10. Once the panna cotta comes down to room temperature, keep the containers in the fridge for 4-5 hours. \n 11. Whip the chilled whipping cream at the lowest speed possible until it s airy and fluffy. You can use a , or ,. \n 12. Switch off before the peaks appear on the cream. Whip for about 1-2 minutes. \n 13. Now add the flavored cream gently and whip it again at the lowest speed for 2-3 minutes. \n 14. Gradually add fruits to the whipped cream and switch off the whipping. Put away in the freezer for at least 2 hours. \n 15. When the panna cotta is set fill the glasses with chilled fruit cream. \n 16. Decorate with some more fruits. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve Mango Panna Cotta With Fruit Cream Recipe chilled after keeping it in the freezer for a few more hours. \n [EOS]

To do this, thoroughly wash the dal and soak in water for 2 hours. \n 2. After two hours, drain the dal completely, put the dal in a mixer-grinder, add chillies, ginger and grind to a coarse paste using very little water (no more than 3 to 4 tablespoons) so that it is thick and crumbly, not runny. \n 3. Add chopped onions, curryleaves, salt and mix well in a bowl. \n 4. Place a kadai on the heat along with enough oil for deep frying. Warm it to smoking point. \n 5. To shape the vadais, first wet your hands. Take a small lump of batter and bind it together between your palms, then flatten it into a 1" round patty using your fingers. \n 6. Slip it gently into hot oil and fry until golden brown on both sides. Fry vadai in batches over moderate heat turning frequently till the Vadai is golden and crisp. \n 7. Drain them on a kitchen towel. \n 8. To prepare the kuzhambu, place a pan over medium heat and warm some oil for tempering in it. \n 9. Add Vadagam (if using) or tempering ingredients and saute lightly for 30 seconds till it starts sputtering. \n 10. When the Vadagam or mustard seeds splutter, add shallots, garlic and curry leaves. Saute for 3 -4 minutes, stirring continuously. \n 11. Add in the tomatoes, salt, coriander powder, chilli powder and toss together for another 1-2 minutes. When tomatoes become mushy add tamarind pulp/juice and combine into a thick sauce like consistency. \n 12. If you are adding pulp, then add 2 cup of water. \n 13. Mix well and simmer over low heat for 15 minutes, stirring occassionally. \n 14. Meanwhile, grind together the ingredients listed under masala paste into a smooth mix, in a mixer-grinder. Gently mix in the prepared paste into the simmering kuzhambu and simmer over low heat for 3 to 4 minutes, till well blended. \n 15. Next, add the Vadai one by one into the kuzhambu and simmer for just 2 minutes. Switch off. \n 16. Masala Vadai Kuzhambu is ready to be. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** served with piping hot steamed rice and a dollop of ghee. \n [EOS]

[BOS] \n **Title:** How To Make Homemade Rose Syrup Recipe \n  \n **Cuisine:** Indian | **Diet:** Vegetarian | **Time:** 15 mins total \n  \n **Ingredients:** \n - Ingredients not specified \n  \n **Instructions:** \n 1. we will first clean and dry the fresh rose petals. Skip the following process if you are using store bought dried rose petals. \n 2. If they are fresh petals then clean rose petals in running water. Dry the rose petals completely and place them on kitchen paper towels. We will dry the rose petals in room temperature on the paper towels. The process of drying will take a couple of days. After a couple of days, you will notice the rose petals have become crisp and dry. When you touch them they will break apart. \n 3. Once the petals are dry, we are ready to make the rose syrup. If you bought the store bought petals you can use it at this stage. \n 4. Boil the water in a saucepan. Place the petals in a glass bowl and pour the boiled water on top of the petals, stir for a few seconds. Allow the rose petals to rest in the water until the water cools down. Once the petals cool down, refrigerate the petals and water filled bowl for 12 to 15 hours. \n 5. Next day, strain the water into a saucepan (your rose water will be dark red). Place the saucepan on medium heat. Add the sugar and clove to the rose water. Keep stirring to dissolve the sugar. As it heats up you will the water frothing on the top. Gradually the foam will go away as the water begins to boil. Once the water begins to boil, turn the heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes and turn off the heat. \n 6. Allow the Rose Syrup to cool completely. The syrup will thicken as it cools down. \n 7. The Rose Syrup is now ready to be used in Ice creams, Milkshakes or Juices or even the classic Rose Milk. You can store the Rose Syrup in a glass bottle and refrigerate it for atleast 2 months. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve hot and enjoy! \n [EOS]

The process of sprouting will take at least 12 hours based on the size of the grain or legume. \n 4. [BOS] \n **Title:** French Brioche Recipe (Savoury Version) \n  \n **Cuisine:** Indian | **Diet:** Vegetarian | **Time:** 180 mins prep, 70 mins cook \n  \n **Ingredients:** \n - All Purpose Flour (Maida) \n - Salt \n - Sugar \n - Whole Eggs \n - Milk \n - Milk \n - Sunflower Oil \n  \n **Instructions:** \n 1. To prepare French Brioche Recipe (Savoury Version). \n 2. Pour Luke warm milk in a bowl, add sugar and yeast into the milk and mix well. Leave it for 10 minutes until the mixture froths up to proof. If it does not froth, discard the mixture and make a new batch again. \n 3. Break the eggs into another bowl and beat them lightly. Set aside. \n 4. Mix flour and salt in a large mixing bowl. Make a depression in the center, pour in the eggs, melted butter and yeast mixture. Knead into smooth dough by adding additional water until pliable and soft. \n 5. Transfer the dough to a clean surface, dust little flour and knead for about 20 minutes until the dough is smooth and shiny. \n 6. Make a ball, and transfer to the same bowl in which you started, grease the bowl and the dough with olive oil. \n 7. Cover the dough with a damp cloth and leave it to prove for an hour or until the size of the dough is doubled in volume. \n 8. After the dough has risen to double the volume, Punch the dough and knead it again. Divide the dough into 4 portions. \n 9. Take one of the portions and roll it into a circle that is 2 mm thick like chapati. I used a plate to cut the round shape from the dough, so all my 4 portions are equal in size. \n 10. Grease the baking tray with olive oil and place the rolled dough on the baking tray. Spread pizza sauce on top of the rolled dough, leaving the edges. \n 11. Next take the second portion of the dough and roll it to the same size. Lift the roll carefully and place it on top of the first layer. Spread pizza sauce on top leaving the edges, like you did for the first layer. \n 12. Repeat step the same steps for two more layers. Do not spread the pizza sauce on top of the 4 th and final layer. \n 13. Place a very small bowl or the mouth of a glass at the center of the layers. Using a sharp knife, slit the layers of dough sheets together into 4 (in a plus shape but leaving the center intact). Next cut in between the 4 portions and make 8 divisions(in a plus shape but leaving the center intact). Finally cut in between the 8 portions making 16 wedges throughout. \n 14. Like a braid, take two adjacent wedges and place each wedge on the opposite side and twist further till centre and form the petal in the centre. Similarly braid every 2 adjacent wedges by twisting and making a flower formation at the end of the work. Seal the edges when you are at the end of every braid twist. \n 15. Cover the flower with damp cloth and let it prove for another 30 minutes. Brush milk over the dough very gently without putting pressure. \n 16. Bake in a pre-heated oven at 180 degrees for 18 to 20 minutes or until the top is golden brown and the bottom edges are brown. Place on wire rack and immediately brush with olive oil and let cool. \n 17. Beautiful French Brioche Recipe (Savoury V. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve hot and enjoy! \n [EOS]

I have used this peeler which makes juliennes for zucchini, papaya, radish and carrots. \n 2. Take some fresh beans and trim its ends and then cut them into 1 inch pieces. \n 3. Take thai red birds eye chilli and chop it finely and place it in a mortar along with clove of garlic. With the help of a pestle crush it and grind it into a paste. If you don't have mortar and pestle you can use a food processor. \n 4. Add the chilli garlic paste into a , and add some lemon juice to it. Also add fish sauce, if you are a vegetarian or don't like the smell of fish sauce you can replace it with soya sauce. Also add brown sugar or palm sugar to the lemon sauce and mix everything together. You can add dried shrimps at this stage for an authentic flavour but if you are a vegetarian you can give it a pass. \n 5. Place the chopped beans in the mortar and bruise them slightly with the pestle so that the juices can run out and it can absorb the dressing better. Take tomato and scoop out its pulp using a spoon. Cut the tomato into juliennes or into cubes, as you like. \n 6. Add the papaya juliennes to the dressing bowl along with beans and tomato. Toss everything together and transfer it to a serving bowl. \n 7. Toss on top toasted salted peanuts. If you like you can crush the peanuts I just used them halved. Indulge in the most amazing and healthy salad from Thailand. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve Thai Som Tum Recipe as a side dish along with , and Steamed Rice for a weekend dinner. \n [EOS]

Garnish with coriander leaves and switch off heat. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve Pachai Sundakkai Puli Kuzhambu Recipe (Turkey Berry Tamarind Based Gravy) with , , , to make it a complete meal. \n [EOS]

[BOS] \n **Title:** Gur Paare Recipe (A traditional Punjabi Wedding Sweet) \n  \n **Cuisine:** Indian | **Diet:** Vegetarian | **Time:** 15 mins total \n  \n **Ingredients:** \n - All Purpose Flour (Maida) \n - Jaggery \n - Fennel seeds (Saunf) \n - Oil \n  \n **Instructions:** \n 1. To begin making the Gur Paare Recipe in a large mixing bowl add the maida and the melted ghee. \n 2. Keep mixing the flour and ghee mixture until you get coarse crumb like texture and the ghee starts to hold the flour together. At this point add teaspoons of water at a time and knead it to make a firm dough. \n 3. Divide the dough in four parts and roll each portion of the dough into a half an inch thick round circle. Cut them into vertical strips and then into 2-3 inch long strips. Repeat for rest of the dough portions. \n 4. In a kadai, heat oil for deep frying on medium heat. Once the oil is hot, add the cut dough strips and fry until slightly brown and crisp. Do make sure to fry on medium heat so it gets crisp evenly. \n 5. Drain them on a kitchen towel and allow them to cool a bit. \n 6. In another heavy bottomed pan, add chopped or grated jaggery. On a slow flame allow it to melt, stirring continuously all the time. \n 7. Cook till you attain the consistency where you add a drop of jaggery into the cool water and it solidifies. \n 8. At this point add the saunf and stir. Turn off the heat and immediately add the fried strips to the jaggery syrup. Mix quickly using two ladles so that all the strips are evenly coated with the jaggery. Once done, the Gur Paare is ready. \n 9. Transfer the Gur Paare onto a tray cool completely. Once completely cool separate the strips carefully taking care not to break them too much. Store them an airtight container for 15 days. \n  \n **Serving Suggestion:** Serve the Gur Paare for festivals like Karva Chauth or any other special occasion in the family. \n [EOS]
